#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set by the harness}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=harness > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid

content.text:
The test passes.

## Summary

The change request — "filter by two things at once (e.g. active projects with a certain label)" — was mostly wired up already: the `/api/projects` endpoint and `ProjectService.list` correctly combine the `status` and `tagId` filters with `AND`, the seed path handles `tags`/`projectTags`, and the UI had both `project-status-filter` and `project-tag-filter` selects.

The failing piece was a **frontend race**. Selecting the status filter and then the tag filter in quick succession fires two overlapping `GET /api/projects` requests. The narrower combined response (1 row) could land first, then the earlier status-only response (2 rows) would resolve and clobber it — so the list settled on 2 rows instead of 1.

The fix in `src/main/frontend/features/projects/ProjectsPage.tsx` tags each fetch with a monotonic sequence number (`loadSeq` ref) and applies only the latest response, discarding stale ones. This keeps the change additive and local to the feature, touches no `data-testid`, and needed no schema or server changes (verified the backend returns exactly the one `Alpha` row for `status=ACTIVE&tagId=1`).

Test result: `1 passed`.
